title: Escape New Years | Armageddon: Chain Of Events

sense.text: “Why baptizest thou then, if thou be not that Christ, nor Elias, neither that prophet?” There was no prophecy that the Messiah would come baptizing with water. The baptism they were referring to was the one prophesied: he would baptize the people, but not with water, with something else.
“I baptize with water: but there standeth one among you, whom ye know not”. John was doing it with water, so they thought he must be him. John told them the one coming after him is the one.

precepts.why: “I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance: but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire”. It was believed by them that the Messiah would come to baptize, so they said, okay, so you’re the guy. And he’s like no, the one after me is going to come and baptize you with the Holy Ghost and with fire. Because John was doing it with water, they thought he must be the Christ.

sense.text: “And the passover, a feast of the Jews, was nigh”: the passover was coming close.
“Whence shall we buy bread, that these may eat?” He was testing Philip with that question.

“And this he said to prove him: for he himself knew what he would do.” Christ knew what he was going to do, but he wanted to see what Philip thought. He was testing his disciples, just to see where their minds were. He was proving them.

Philip answered that “Two hundred pennyworth of bread is not sufficient for them”, and Andrew found a lad with “five barley loaves, and two small fishes: but what are they among so many?” So he was simply proving them, to see what their thoughts were on how to feed the people.

He made the men sit down, “about five thousand”, distributed the loaves and the fishes “as much as they would”, and they “filled twelve baskets with the fragments of the five barley loaves”. That was the miracle that was performed, but the point of the question was proving the disciples, to see what their mind was on how to feed the people.

There’s no history on Janus, but there are precepts for it. “And he shall speak great words against the most High, and shall wear out the saints of the most High”. Who’s the he? He is Esau, our enemies, the nations.

“And think to change times and laws”. The heathens thought to change times. People always say times change. Times don’t change: the sun and the moon always come out the same exact time they’re supposed to come out. He shall think to change times and laws, because there will come a time when our people would come to understand that he has changed times and laws, and we’re going to follow God according to the laws of God, the times according to the laws of God.

The months of the year are based upon Rome, and so are the planets of the solar system, because America is an extension of Rome. January goes back to the god Janus, the god of beginnings and endings, a two-headed or two-faced god, because he’s the beginning and he’s the end. February is named after the Roman festival of purification, februa, the month of cleansing, and the custom of Lupercalia was done in that month, which is what Valentine’s Day is based upon: fornication beyond understanding. March is Mars, the Roman god of war. May is Maia, the goddess of growth, because that’s springtime. June is Juno, the goddess of marriage, childbirth and protection, wife of Jupiter. July goes back to Julius Caesar, and August to Augustus Caesar; before it was called August it was called Sextilis, which means six.

Septem is Latin for seven, octo is eight (an octagon has eight sides, an octopus has eight arms), novem is nine, and dec is ten, as in decade and decalogue. So how can December be the 12th month when dec is 10? How can October be the 10th month when octo is 8? Start from late March, early April and see how it all falls in place: March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November, December. December is 10, January is 11, February is 12. January and February are the last months of the year.

That’s why Janus is the god of beginnings and endings: in the eyes of God that’s the end of the year, but Esau makes it the beginning of the year. Two faces for confusion. For the Jews this is towards the end of our year; we’re approaching a new beginning of our year, which will be late March, early April. There’s no way in hell that this is the beginning of the year. It don’t make no damn sense; it don’t even make sense when you count the numbers. That’s why it says he shall think to change times and laws. You can think to when you deceive the people, but when a brother of God comes out, it clears all the confusion up.

precepts.why: “This month shall be unto you the beginning of months: it shall be the first month of the year to you.” This is God’s new year: this month, he says, shall be the beginning of months, the first month of the year to you.

“This day came ye out in the month Abib.” He names the month: Abib is the first month of the year unto us. Abib means ear of corn; that’s when the spring begins. Write this down: it falls between late March and early April. That’s a precept, and historically it falls between late March and early April.

“Observe the month of Abib, and keep the passover unto the Lord thy God”: that feast day falls in the first month of our year. “For in the month of Abib the Lord thy God brought thee forth out of Egypt by night.” The Lord brought us forth out of Egypt in that month by night, which is the beginning of our year.

Read again after the months were counted out: Passover is our first feast day of the year because it falls in the first month of the year. So there’s no way this is the beginning of the year.

Why will he only think to change times and laws? This is why he won’t be able to do it fully: “Truth shall spring out of the earth; and righteousness shall look down from heaven.” He will think to change times and laws but not be successful in doing so fully. The remnant of our people will wake up in this earth and spread the truth that this is complete and utter stupidness and confusion.

sense.text:
The Muslims do not have the same Torah we have. They may have read from the same Torah as us back then, but they did not believe what they were reading, because they profess that Ishmael is the chosen child, and that’s not what the Torah says.

“Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read: no one of these shall fail”: these is the prophecies. “None shall want her mate”. What is a mate? A companion. None shall want, or lack, her mate: no one is going to need to mate another book with the Bible. The Bible needs no mate; there’s nothing to add to it. The Muslims believe the Quran is the word of God and the Bible is a confirmation of the Quran, so the Bible is the Quran’s add-on, as opposed to the Quran being the Bible’s add-on. There’s a problem with that.

“For my mouth it hath commanded”: the words of the Bible, God’s mouth commanded them. “And his spirit it hath gathered them”: his spirit gathered the words of the prophets.

“And he hath cast the lot for them, and his hand hath divided it unto them by line: they shall possess it for ever”: the Bible. “From generation to generation shall they dwell therein”: you shall dwell in this book.

This shows the difference between what the Muslims profess to have and what the Bible says. “This is my covenant, which ye shall keep, between me and you and thy seed after thee; Every man child among you shall be circumcised.” Abraham had a lot of servants living in his house, 318 servants. He had a huge house; he was a very wealthy and powerful man, referred to as a prince. “And it shall be a token of the covenant betwixt me and you”: between God and Abraham.

“He that is born in the house, or bought with money of any stranger, which is not of thy seed”: strangers are not of your people, but in your house they shall be circumcised also. Your rules, your house; that’s what he’s saying. “And my covenant shall be in your flesh for an everlasting covenant.” The uncircumcised man child, “that soul shall be cut off from his people; he hath broken my covenant.”
Sarai’s name becomes Sarah. “I will bless her, and give thee a son also of her”: she becomes “a mother of nations; kings of people shall be of her.”

“Shall a child be born unto him that is an hundred years old? and shall Sarah, that is ninety years old, bear?” She was ten years younger than him. We’re senior citizens, we’re old, we’re going to have kids?
“O that Ishmael might live before thee!” Ishmael was his firstborn son, that he had with the Egyptian woman, Sarah’s handmaid Hagar. Abraham said, but what about Ishmael, will he live before thee?

“Sarah thy wife shall bear thee a son indeed; and thou shalt call his name Isaac”: your wife Sarah is going to bring forth a child aside from Ishmael. “I will establish my covenant with him for an everlasting covenant, and with his seed after him.” In the Quran they state that this is in reference to Ishmael, that he will be the one God made a covenant with. That’s not what the Bible says.

What they’ll say to you is the Bible’s been corrupted, that it was corrupted to make it seem as if Isaac was the chosen and not Ishmael. According to them the Bible is corrupt and you can’t trust it, and Ishmael was the chosen one.

“And as for Ishmael, I have heard thee: Behold, I have blessed him, and will make him fruitful, and will multiply him exceedingly; twelve princes shall he beget, and I will make him a great nation. But my covenant will I establish with Isaac”. With who? With Isaac, “which Sarah shall bear unto thee at this set time in the next year.”

Abraham circumcised Ishmael and all that were born in his house, “in the selfsame day”. Abraham was “ninety years old and nine” and Ishmael was “thirteen years old” when he was circumcised. So by this point Ishmael was circumcised, but the covenant was made with Isaac.

precepts.why:
Fast forward to Isaac: “Abraham circumcised his son Isaac being eight days old, as God had commanded him.” Abraham was circumcised at 99, and he was “an hundred years old, when his son Isaac was born unto him.”

Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, Ishmael, “mocking”, mocking Isaac, and said “Cast out this bondwoman and her son: for the son of this bondwoman shall not be heir with my son, even with Isaac.” Get rid of Hagar and Ishmael, both of them. There can only be one heir. “And the thing was very grievous in Abraham’s sight because of his son.” God told him “Let it not be grievous in thy sight because of the lad, and because of thy bondwoman; in all that Sarah hath said unto thee, hearken unto her voice; for in Isaac shall thy seed be called.” That goes back to Genesis 17: Isaac is the one he chose.

“And also of the son of the bondwoman will I make a nation, because he is thy seed.” So he did bless them as a nation. They are very blessed: they got wealth, they got oil, they got the land. They’re not doing too good right now in Palestine, because Israel is stepping on them over there, but outside of Palestine they’re doing very well for themselves, an abundance of oil and gold and wealth; one of the wealthiest men alive is an Arab. God bless them. Look at Dubai: their cop cars are Bugattis, and they ride around with lions in their cars.

Abraham gave Hagar bread and a bottle of water, “and sent her away: and she departed, and wandered in the wilderness of Beer–sheba.”

After Sarah dies, Abraham remarries. “Then again Abraham took a wife, and her name was Keturah.” Keturah gave birth to more kids of Abraham, “Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah”: all different so-called Arab nations, and they ended up moving in the east, so those became more so-called Arabs as well. But the wild ones, the ones that blow things up, is Ishmael: the alphas of the Arabs. In the history books the wild Arabs were called the Bedouin. There are different tribes and sects of Arabs in Arabia.

Keturah was a concubine and Hagar was a concubine; see what happened to them. “But unto the sons of the concubines, which Abraham had, Abraham gave gifts, and sent them away from Isaac his son”, because they cannot be heirs with his son, “while he yet lived, eastward, unto the east country”: into the so-called Middle East, the Near East, the Sahara, that area over there, and they resided there.

Now the Muslims say the Bible has been corrupted. But in their own book, Muhammad and them sat down with the Jews and learned from the Jews, and the Jews at that time had the same Bible we have now. Their own book says, ‘O people of the Book, you have nothing to stand on unless you observe the Torah.’ People of the Book, that’s us: Muhammad talking to the Jews and the Christians, the same people, who had the Bible during that time. If the Torah is corrupted, why would he tell us to stand on it? It makes no damn sense. We have our Torah, the first five books of Moses, and we have the Gospel, the Old Testament and the New, so what we need that book for?

sense.text:
A lot of them Muslims you battling at work don’t even know their own book that they believe in, but this is where we got it from. “Lift up thine eyes unto the high places, and see where thou hast not been lien with”: we was always in captivity, always being possessed by the other nations because of our wickedness.

“In the ways hast thou sat for them, as the Arabian in the wilderness”. When did we sit for the Arabs in the wilderness? That’s the Arab slave trade, a pivotal part of history you got to know. “And thou hast polluted the land with thy whoredoms and with thy wickedness.” Them Negroes you battling at your job don’t even know that that’s where we got it from. Mecca was one of the largest slave ports, one of the worst; that’s where they castrated us. They forced that religion on us. Islam was forced on us just like Christianity was forced on us. Philly is heavily involved in that nonsense, Baltimore too.

Jeremiah 3 says we sat for the Arabs in the wilderness to learn from them, to be taught the law. Their own book asks why the Jews come to them for judgment, ‘when they already have the Torah’. So their book tells us to follow our book. If your book says one thing and mine says another, one of them got to be wrong, but your book is telling me to follow my own book, so I’m going to follow my book and not yours.

Attacking Islam is not a personal issue with our people who are in Islam. The problem is with the people that established it, because they were heavily rooted and involved in our enslavement, and their Quran allows and justifies them having us as slaves in portions of Africa and Arab countries today, openly and secretly: Libya, Mauritania, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, and the European Union knows about it and they all profit from it. They bought brothers from Ethiopia as slaves, castrated from about age eight, and set them to watch over Muhammad’s grave; the more you were castrated, the more you were worth as a slave. That’s why there is no mercy for it: it was very destructive to our people on all levels.

“There is an exquisite subtilty”: someone that’s very subtle, slick, cunning, hunting, like how Satan was with Eve, subtle. “And the same is unjust”: that person who is exquisitely subtle is unjust.

“And there is one that turneth aside to make judgment appear”: one that deals with things righteously, to reveal judgment. One is slick and cunning and subtle; the other exposes things. “And there is a wise man that justifieth in judgment.”
Verse 26 elaborates on that exquisite subtlety: a wicked man that hangs down his head sadly, but is “full of deceit”.

How can you be sure the Lord is pleased with you serving him? “Unto you therefore, O kings, do I speak, that ye may learn wisdom, and not fall away. For they that keep holiness holily shall be judged holy: and they that have learned such things shall find what to answer.” When you keep that which is holy and remain holy, you learn what to answer: your understanding starts to increase, you increase in this truth, you become more enlightened. “Wherefore set your affection upon my words; desire them, and ye shall be instructed.”

“To think therefore upon her is perfection of wisdom: and whoso watcheth for her shall quickly be without care. For she goeth about seeking such as are worthy of her”. “The very true beginning of her is the desire of discipline; and the care of discipline is love; And love is the keeping of her laws; and the giving heed unto her laws is the assurance of incorruption”. One of the main things you’re going to notice about yourself is that you increase in understanding.

It won’t be like, oh wow, God did this. It takes time before you start noticing those things. People are going to rely on you; you’ll be allowed into circles you weren’t allowed in before, among the great men, the leadership, the captains. When your reputation precedes you, when you are sought after among your superiors and they say that’s a good brother right there, put him over this office, that’s a clear sign the Most High is starting to bless you and deal with you.

precepts.why:
“Consider that I laboured not for myself only, but for all them that seek learning.” Once you increase in understanding, you begin to acquire the understanding that you are not only learning for yourself but for them that seek learning. You grow and flourish; you learn to teach your people. Things become easy to you and become more clear through repetition and experience.

“Hear me, O ye great men of the people, and hearken with your ears, ye rulers of the congregation.” Over time you become a great man among the people, a ruler of the congregation: you gain a certain level of promotion, like an officer or a captain or a deacon or a bishop. That comes with time and experience, but it comes after the things earlier: desiring wisdom and seeking her.

“If thou be among great men, make not thyself equal with them; and when ancient men are in place, use not many words.” You begin to learn discretion, to conduct yourself properly among the people, and you teach the people discretion. Discretion is growth. You grow over time, and that’s how you start to realize the Most High is dealing with you.

sense.text:
How do you deal with the pressure of men relying on you without burning out? “There is that destroyeth his own soul through bashfulness”. Bashfulness is acting like a yellow belly, scared, a pushover. Brothers are given certain tasks and they take it on: I’ll do that, I can do that too, I’ll do that too. They overwhelm themselves, and they don’t say no. That’s a bashful spirit.

“And by accepting of persons overthroweth himself”: he doesn’t want to displease the leading officer or ranking member over him, so he says okay even when he knows he can’t handle all that load at one time. Brothers break down and fall apart when they take on too much and say nothing. Not that they’re weak or effeminate; they don’t want to step on any toes or seem unreliable. It’s not that you’re unreliable; you just have too much on your plate. You have to learn to distribute that burden.

“There is that for bashfulness promiseth to his friend”, or to a leading officer over him, or a brother, “and maketh him his enemy for nothing.” You become unreliable, and now he’s mad at you for nothing. You could have said, I can’t do it. You got to learn how to balance what you can and cannot do.

precepts.why:
“The thing that thou doest is not good.” Moses was taking on a lot more than he could bear: I can handle all these millions of people on my own. Jethro, his father-in-law, was a priest of Midian, so he had experience in priesthood, and he said Moses, man, what you’re doing is stupid. “Thou wilt surely wear away, both thou, and this people that is with thee: for this thing is too heavy for thee; thou art not able to perform it thyself alone.” You’ll destroy yourself.

“Hearken now unto my voice, I will give thee counsel”. Teach them the ordinances and laws, and “provide out of all the people able men, such as fear God, men of truth, hating covetousness; and place such over them, to be rulers of thousands, and rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens”. Jethro was telling him to learn how to delegate, to share the load. That’s the answer: you cannot do it on your own.

Burnout comes from taking on more than you can and being too bashful to admit it. If you feel like crap because you’re just lazy, that’ll reveal itself. But if you’re carrying a lot on your plate, it’s best to say something: listen, I need help. A lot of brothers have that spirit, I’m a man, I’ll do it on my own. That’s pride. That was Moses being prideful. Set up men under you to help you; that’s how you avoid the burnout.

sense.text: What anchors hold you down when you’re going through a trial? “Then they that feared the Lord spake often one to another: and the Lord hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared the Lord, and that thought upon his name.” You got to learn to communicate. Going through a trial, you talk to people. Delegation, communication, conversation: all those are pivotal in this truth, communicating with your brothers. If you stay doing your own thing in your own head, you fall.

precepts.why: “Say not, I have enough for my life.” Then: “Follow not thine own mind and thy strength, to walk in the ways of thy heart”. That’s what you don’t do when you go through a trial. People going through a trial end up in their head, always in their own mind. Over time you overthink things, or you don’t think at all and you’re just emotional, leaning one way or the other, because you’re not talking to nobody.

sense.text:
“Extol not thyself in the counsel of thine own heart”: extol, or exalt, not yourself in the counsel of your own mind, “that thy soul be not torn in pieces as a bull straying alone.” A bull alone has no protection, no one to help him. In a herd, the one that veers off is not in communication with everybody else; he’s on his own, in his own head, drinking water over there by himself, and the lion looks at him and says look at this stupid one, I’m gonna eat him alive. That’s Satan.

When you stay alone in your own head for a long period of time, Satan starts to play with you. You hear a thought in your mind saying they hate you, they don’t like you, they’re being too rough, they didn’t hear your side. Meanwhile you hear the scriptures being read and you get it, but a voice says that’s not what that really means, that’s a misinterpretation. That’s Satan playing with you. Satan tries to convince you that those who love you and care for you are the ones against you, trying to destroy you. If it’s not in your head, it comes out of your spouse’s mouth.

Why is your soul torn in pieces? Because after a while the understanding that you have begins to be ripped away, torn away in pieces over time.

When you’re going through it and you’re dead wrong, there’s nothing to say. There will be times you may have a valid point, but at that moment when you’re wrong, nothing you say matters. Fix yourself, and after the smoke has settled and they see the brother or sister is trying to recover, then you can say what you meant and be listened to. When you go home and tell yourself that ain’t fair, they didn’t let me talk, that’s Satan talking to you: see, they don’t want to hear the scriptures, they wrong. That’s a very scary place to be, because you all alone. Satan seems to be in full effect late at night, around 2, 3, 4 in the morning, when you’re to yourself and everyone is asleep; brothers who fall into their lust often fall around that time.

“Thou shalt eat up thy leaves”: your leaves is your understanding. You turn on what you’ve learned. You start to say maybe nations can’t be saved, them guys are a cult, they’re trying to control me, all nations can be saved, I got good white friends at work, I can have more than one wife, I make six figures. You start hearing stupid stuff in your head. It sounds like you, but it’s not you. “And lose thy fruit”: you lose your understanding because you’re alone in here. “And leave thyself as a dry tree”: all the water, the understanding, is gone.

“A wicked soul shall destroy him that hath it”: him that strays alone, eats his own leaves up, loses his fruit and becomes a dry tree becomes a wicked soul. If your soul is torn in pieces, you become a wicked soul. “And shall make him to be laughed to scorn of his enemies.” The enemies are the brothers we once called brothers. Now you doing videos, why I left, I left the cult, and we laugh at you. They all do the same thing: those who leave and become a bull straying alone always find each other, and over time they turn on each other, because they all got that alone spirit. They all say I don’t believe in elders, I don’t believe in rank, we’re all equal in God. Meanwhile Paul said it clear: God the Father, the Son, man, woman and child, order. When they leave, God don’t care about order, we’re all elders. Your soul is ripped to pieces, now you’re a dry tree with a video that got two views, one view, his grandma watching. That is the aftermath of staying alone and exalting your own self in your mind.

“Sweet language will multiply friends”. Sweet language goes back to Malachi 3:16: communication. It multiplies friends, because brother, if you don’t talk, nobody knows you; if you just sit there quiet looking around, you look like a damn agent. “And a fair-speaking tongue will increase kind greetings”: you end up respected and reputable. Communication is key.

“Be in peace with many: nevertheless have but one counsellor of a thousand.” It goes into counsel because if you don’t do these things it leads back to verse two: exalt yourself in your own counsel, stray alone, eat your leaves, lose your fruit, become a dry tree, become a wicked soul, laughed to scorn by enemies. That is the end result of not fulfilling verses 5 and 6. If you’re not fulfilling 5 and 6, Satan becomes your counsellor, and you become 2, 3 and 4.

precepts.why: Where are you straying at? In your own head, in your own mind, all over the place. “Be sober, be vigilant”: how are you sober and mindful? When you’re around other vigilant and mindful brothers that you’re in communication with. “Because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”. Who does the lion seek to devour? The bulls that stray alone, that do their own thing.

“Be stedfast in thy understanding”: be steadfast in what you’ve learned. “And let thy word be the same”: let your words be the same, coming out of the Bible. “Be swift to hear”: in your own head you ain’t listening; you’re listening to somebody, but it ain’t coming from here. “And let thy life be sincere”: be honest with yourself. Am I right in this? All the witnesses say no; three, four counsellor brothers are saying bro, you’re going off, and you’re like nah, you guys are wrong. You’re straying alone.

“And with patience give answer.” The less you talk the better; the more you talk, the more you end yourself. Sometimes it’s best just to listen, take heed, listen with patience. You got to learn to use discretion.

sense.text:
A man in Texas calling himself a doctor in his church said Mark 16:18 was being done in his church, healing people, and even raising somebody from the dead. Where was he during Covid? We here in New York and you ain’t never come here and raised nobody up.

Mark 16:18 was fulfilled with Paul: “there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand”, and the barbarians said “No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he hath escaped the sea, yet vengeance suffereth not to live.” “And he shook off the beast into the fire, and felt no harm.” They looked when he should have swollen or fallen down dead, and when no harm came to him, “they changed their minds, and said that he was a god.”

Now these churches have healing services where they throw a jacket around and everybody falls back. They should throw some serpents in there too and see what happens. A pastor in some country had a serpent, and it bit him, and he ain’t do too good. Tell him try that.

“Woe be to fearful hearts, and faint hands, and the sinner that goeth two ways!” The sinner that goes two ways is one whose faith is wavering. He’s trying to play both sides of the fence: he believes on one hand, and on the other he don’t. One foot in the world and one foot in the truth. Revelation calls it lukewarm.

I believe I’m an Israelite, but I’m going to celebrate Christmas. I believe, but I’m going to celebrate New Year. You take your fringes and ribbon of blue off, wear a plain shirt and go to Times Square with your family and watch the ball drop, but you know you’re Israel and you should be in here. You’re at your family’s house in front of a stupid Christmas tree with gifts under it, but you know you’re Israel. That’s the sinner that goes two ways.
The thorns on Christ’s head were mockery. “Then Pilate therefore took Jesus, and scourged him”: he got beat, real bad.

“And the soldiers platted a crown of thorns, and put it on his head”: Roman soldiers. They said he was the king, so they gave him a fake crown to mock him, “And said, Hail, King of the Jews! and they smote him with their hands.” A mock crown, to mock him.

Why is our punishment greater than the punishment of Sodom? Because they died once when they got destroyed; we’re going to die again. “And every one that shall be saved, and shall be able to escape by his works, and by faith”: works and faith go hand in hand. They “Shall be preserved from the said perils, and shall see my salvation in my land, and within my borders: for I have sanctified them for me from the beginning.” Those who keep faith and works are those predestined to do so anyway.

“Then shall they be in pitiful case, which now have abused my ways: and they that have cast them away despitefully shall dwell in torments.” “For such as in their life have received benefits, and have not known me”: they heard the word of God and rejected it. “And they that have lothed my law, while they had yet liberty, and, when as yet place of repentance was open unto them, understood not, but despised it”.
“The same must know it after death by pain.” That’s why it’s worse than Sodom for them: after death by pain. That’s the hellfire Christ talked about all the time, the second death.

Why did David take Michal back after Saul gave her to another man; wouldn’t that be adultery? No, because she didn’t sleep with him, and she was already promised to David. “For as an angel of God, so is my lord the king to discern good and bad”: as an angel of God he can discern good and bad.

“Is not the hand of Joab with thee in all this?” Joab sent this woman to speak on his behalf, and David wasn’t there, but the Lord revealed it to him. “Thy servant Joab, he bade me, and he put all these words in the mouth of thine handmaid”. “And my lord is wise, according to the wisdom of an angel of God, to know all things that are in the earth.” Joab killed Abner, in the fifth rib, and David knew about that too.

So when Michal was given over to someone else, David had already killed 200 Philistines for their foreskins, the dowry for her in marriage. Saul said kill these Philistines and bring back the foreskins, thinking David would be killed by them, but he didn’t die. A deal’s a deal; the dowry is a dowry. She was promised to him first, she belonged to him, and he knew she wasn’t defiled yet, so he went and took back what was his. It wasn’t adultery.

precepts.why: “But Saul had given Michal his daughter, David’s wife, to Phalti the son of Laish, which was of Gallim.” She was given to another man, but she was David’s wife already, promised to him first.

sense.text: When you read the scriptures, sometimes the answer is in the verse above the verse, under the verse, or the chapter after. You got to learn to read through it. “Whoso killeth any person, the murderer shall be put to death by the mouth of witnesses: but one witness shall not testify against any person to cause him to die.” Two or three witnesses. Moreover you shall take no satisfaction for the life of a murderer: if you kill someone, you get killed with the death.

“The generations of the sons of Noah, Shem, Ham, and Japheth”: yes, the sons of these generations become nations. They gave birth to multiples of nations. Shem gave birth to the Assyrians, Syrians, Elamites, Moabites, Ammonites and Israelites. Japheth gave birth to the Javanites: Germany, Greece, Rome, the Etruscans, the Minoans. Ham is explanatory: Hamites, Ethiopians, Egyptians, Canaanites, Libyans, Somalians.

All Israelites are descendants of Abraham, and so were these Ishmeelites. “Behold, a company of Ishmeelites came from Gilead with their camels”. Judah said “let us sell him to the Ishmeelites, and let not our hand be upon him; for he is our brother and our flesh.” Yes, Joseph’s brothers were having a conversation about selling him to the Ishmeelites.

“Then there passed by Midianites merchantmen; and they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver”. The Midianites took him out and sold him to the Ishmeelites. They worked together; they didn’t just happen to find him. They were always into slave trading, Ishmael and Midian. Ishmael comes from Abraham, and Midian comes from his wife Keturah; they both come from Abraham. They were together when they took him and sold him into slavery.

“Because ye believed me not, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel, therefore ye shall not bring this congregation into the land which I have given them.” Moses sanctified him not; verse 10 shows what that means.

precepts.why: “Hear now, ye rebels; must we fetch you water out of this rock?” God didn’t like that: must we fetch you water. He didn’t give God the glory at that point, because he was angry. Moses spoke angrily, and the Most High said, hey, you mean must you fetch water out of the rock? He spoke unadvisedly. That’s what it means by not sanctifying him in the eyes of the children of Israel.

sense.text: This is not the same leviathan mentioned in the book of Job. This leviathan is Esau. Babylon had the lion, Persia had the bear, the Greeks had the leopard, and the Lord gave Esau a bunch of ensigns, so demonic, like 80 ensigns; the first ensign he gave him was the eagle. “In that day the Lord with his sore and great and strong sword shall punish leviathan the piercing serpent, even leviathan that crooked serpent; and he shall slay the dragon that is in the sea.”

precepts.why: “Thou brakest the heads of the dragons in the waters.” “Thou brakest the heads of leviathan in pieces, and gavest him to be meat to the people inhabiting the wilderness.” There’s more than one head on this leviathan. The leviathan in Job has one head; this one has more than one head because it’s a dragon. And he shall be meat for us when we’re ruling in the kingdom; that’s what they’re talking about.

That’s why it says heads, plural: “behold a great red dragon”, the leviathan, “having seven heads and ten horns, and seven crowns upon his heads.” Isaiah 27:1 precepts with Psalms 74:13-14 and Revelation 12: the leviathan is Esau, the great red dragon.

sense.text: If you’ve self-examined and made a list of sin issues to work on, what’s the most effective method? Meditation; Bishop brought this out to us before. “And Isaac went out to meditate in the field at the eventide”.

precepts.why: “When I remember thee upon my bed, and meditate on thee in the night watches.” As Isaac did in the eventide. One of the things we’re told to do is examine each sin that we deal with, take the scriptures that deal with each one, and meditate upon them for a certain amount of time, alone to yourself, speaking to the Lord.

sense.text: This is how you identify the sin you’re dealing with. “Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth; fornication”: you identify that you’re dealing with the spirit of fornication. “Uncleanness, inordinate affection”: you got inordinate affection inside of you. “Evil concupiscence, and covetousness”: you see that you have a covetous spirit. How do you deal with that? The Bible says to mortify it: to kill it, deaden it, get rid of it.

precepts.why:
The way you get rid of it: “But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection”. You examine yourself and see the spirits you’re fighting inside, the lusts, the issues in your spirit, and you bring those things into subjection. That’s the same thing as mortifying your members.

“Lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway.” If you don’t bring it into subjection, after you done taught this gospel, done the street teaching, waking people up, you’re going to be a castaway. You got to fix it. That don’t mean you’re not going to make mistakes.

This is the key thing: “Return unto the Lord, and forsake thy sins, make thy prayer before his face”: ask him for forgiveness. “And offend less.” Sometimes you fight with these things inside of you and you might mess up, but offend less in the sight of God. You want to walk perfect, but brothers and sisters, you all going to make mistakes. Offend less, understanding that you could also be a castaway: the Lord could cast any one of us away if we don’t overcome these things we’re dealing with inside.

It’s the same as the scripture that says don’t add sin to sin. That don’t mean you’re not going to fall, but you have to bring everything you’re fighting into submission to Christ: these thoughts, feelings and emotions, I didn’t feel the judgment was right, I didn’t feel this or that. These are the things that trouble us every day. They’re always going to be there. Your job is to shut them down.

sense.text: These are the events that are going to take place with us, the 12 tribes of Israel, before Christ returns: from captivity to our deliverance. “Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets”. Christ says don’t think I came to destroy the law or anything the prophets said. “I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil”: I came to destroy nothing the prophets say or the law says; I came to fulfil what it says.

“One jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law”. Christ came to take away nothing from the law, and to change nothing the prophets said. Christ did not change anything the prophets said. When he died, everything the prophets said had to be fulfilled: we had to be scattered into slavery, and we had to forget who we are.

precepts.why:
Now see what the prophets said. “And they shall fall by the edge of the sword”: the 12 tribes of Israel are going to fall by the edge of the sword, meaning war. “And shall be led away captive into all nations”: led as slaves into all nations, all over the earth, the four corners of the earth. That’s written in the prophets, and Christ did not come and die to change that. After Christ died we were still enslaved and still scattered throughout the four corners of the earth.

Falling by the edge of the sword goes into when the Romans came against us in 70 AD, but it took a process of time for us to be scattered into all nations. When Rome came against us, a lot of us fled to certain parts of Africa and Arabia. While we were over there they came and made war with us again, and we fell by the edge of the sword again. We warred with the Hamitic tribes, and they enslaved us and sold us to the white man as slaves. The Israelites are the people that were led as slaves into all nations, not the people that were in concentration camps.

“And Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled”: Jerusalem is going to be occupied by Gentiles. The time of the Gentiles is fulfilled when Christ returns. The time we’re living in right now is the time of the Gentiles, which goes back to Daniel’s four kingdoms that rule on this earth: we are in the last one, the fourth beast, the eagle. So the people occupying the land today are Gentiles, not the people of God. That’s Bible prophecy. You can believe the Bible or the so-called white man: the white man says the people in the land are the Jews; the Bible says the Jews are going to be slaves in all nations and the land occupied by Gentiles. The children of the captivity, the people of slavery right through history, that’s the 12 tribes of Israel.

Christ didn’t come to change nothing the prophet said. “I said, I would scatter them into corners”: the prophet said we will be scattered into corners. “I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men”: the remembrance that we are the children of Israel has ceased from among men. Go to the Chinese, the Arabs, anybody, and ask who the children of Israel are: would they point to you so-called Negroes, the North American Indians, the so-called Puerto Ricans? No. The white man did a good job.

You got to be high up in society to have the knowledge that these children of the slave trade are the Israelites. The pope and the Roman Catholic Church know who we are; the presidents and the higher echelon, the spiritual wickedness, the governments that rule this earth, they know who we are. And now the world is knowing who we are, because we are teaching the truth.

Not just men: it has ceased from our own remembrance. We don’t even know who we are; we call ourselves all these different names and titles.

“They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation”. Who said this? The nations. It was a conspiracy why you don’t know who you are; the remembrance of us was ceased on purpose. It was done deliberately, not by mistake: they came together and said let us cut them off, “that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.”

Read again after Job 9:24: that is how the remembrance of us ceased from among men. The nations came together, took crafty counsel, and cut us off from being a nation. That’s why we call ourselves the terms we call ourselves today.

How did they do it? “The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof”. The judges of this earth are the 12 tribes of Israel. He covered the faces of the judges by changing our identity. That’s how the remembrance that we are the children of Israel ceased: the white man, Edom, covered our identity, our faces, and it was done by design.

That’s why in slavery you couldn’t read; they made sure you didn’t know how to read and write. When we came here as slaves we could read and write; we knew who we were. They set up systems to destroy us mentally and teach us lies, and it was done all over Africa too: wherever the children of Israel were as slaves, they came, conquered us and destroyed our identity.

sense.text: “Then said I, Lord, how long? And he answered, Until the cities be wasted without inhabitant”: the cities of Israel have got to be destroyed without inhabitants, none of us living in that land anymore. That’s what you see going on. We not in that land no more; you might have one or two of our brothers over there, but they’re subjugated under Esau. “And the houses without man, and the land be utterly desolate”.

“And the Lord have removed men far away”: the men he’s removing far away are the 12 tribes of Israel, far away into captivity. That goes with ‘I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men.’

“And there be a great forsaking in the midst of the land”: we forsook our identity, we left our culture. We fled the land of Israel from persecution and lived in all these different countries, scattered toward the four corners of the earth in slavery. That’s the great forsaking.

Read it again after Joel 3: we were removed far away by the Africans and the Arabs selling us to the Grecians. That’s what Isaiah is talking about, and the great forsaking in the midst of the land is because of slavery.

precepts.why: This shows how the Israelites were removed far away. “For, behold, in those days, and in that time, when I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem”: Christ is going to bring back the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem, meaning bring us back into our own land.

“The children also of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have ye sold unto the Grecians, that ye might remove them far from their border.” This is Tyre and Zidon, and Palestine. They enslaved us and sold us to the white man to remove us far from our borders. That’s how we are here in America and throughout the Caribbean islands: the Arabs and the Africans sold us to the white man.

“Behold, I will raise them out of the place whither ye have sold them, and will return your recompence upon your own head”: what you did to them is going to be returned on your own head. That’s future prophecy.

“By the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and by our gathering together unto him”: before Christ returns, we will be gathered together unto him. “That ye be not soon shaken in mind, or be troubled, neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter as from us, as that the day of Christ is at hand.” Don’t let nobody tell you the day of Christ is at hand. Paul said this because there were dudes back then teaching that the resurrection had already taken place.

“Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first”. That’s what we read in Isaiah 6: that falling away first is the great forsaking. We had to be led away in slavery into all nations, and the remembrance of us had to cease from among men. Back then, when we were in the land and Christ was there, we knew who we were. The apostles knew: I’m Judah. But prophecy had to be fulfilled, where nobody would look at us and say these are the children of Israel.

In slavery they gave us their ways so we would lose who we are, and that’s the same mindset still. Scattered among the nations, the nations are not going to teach you that you are the children of Israel or that you have to repent as an Israelite; they hide your identity from you. That’s why God keeps sending the prophets to bring you back out of all this captivity.

“Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people”. Remember the remembrance of us was to cease from among men. Who is saying we are not God’s people? The people today, the so-called white man: you’re not the Israelites.

“There it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” How is it being said? That’s us teaching in the streets: yes, we are the sons of the living God, what the hell you talking about. In the place is America, it’s Europe, all these lands where they say you are African-Americans, you are Puerto Ricans, all these names they give us. We are going to rise up and say that we are the sons of the living God.

sense.text: “For my son Jesus shall be revealed with those that be with him”: those with him are the 12 apostles. “And they that remain shall rejoice within four hundred years.”

“After these years shall my son Christ die”: we all know Christ died. Remember, that day shall not come unless there be a falling away first. “And all men that have life”: after Christ died, all men that have life died. The life there is the Holy Spirit, the brothers that understood the scriptures. When the apostles and their disciples died, there was no truth being taught on the earth: bugged-out doctrines were taught for close to 2,000 years. People knew they were Israel, but the true gospel, the understanding the apostles had, nobody had after Christ and the apostles died.

“And the world shall be turned into the old silence seven days, like as in the former judgments: so that no man shall remain”: no man that has the knowledge and understanding of what God requires of us remained.

“And after seven days the world, that yet awaketh not, shall be raised up”. That yet awaketh not is us Israelites that are asleep; we don’t know we are the children of Israel. After a while, the scripture says, we are going to wake up to the truth of who we are. A lot of things took place in that whole time.

“That it shall be for a time, times, and an half”. A time is going into 100 years. Times is two, 200 years: that’s 300. And a half is 50: 350 years. For a time, times and the dividing of times, 350 years, it’s going to be like that: us being destroyed.

“And when he shall have accomplished to scatter the power of the holy people, all these things shall be finished.” The power of the holy people had to be scattered, meaning none of us supposed to be left knowing we are the children of Israel. We had to be scattered throughout the four corners of the earth in captivity and forget our nationality. That goes back to Deuteronomy, when it says your sons and daughters shall be given unto another people and there shall be no might in your hand: we had no power, no army to say let’s go fight against the white man and get back our sons and daughters that were enslaved. The holy people have no power no more, no army, no lands. Our power is the Most High God; that’s who we’re trusting in in these last days.

Once the holy people is scattered, all these things shall be finished. That’s the great falling away: us forgetting who we are, scattered into the corners, the remembrance of us ceased from among men.

“And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city”. Their dead bodies goes back to 2 Esdras, when it says they awake not, and all that have life die, the life being the spirit of Christ, and there would be an old silence. It says dead bodies, but it’s spirit: the Israelites are spiritually dead, not physically dead.

The great city is talking about America; there’s no greater city in the world than America. That’s where the Israelites’ dead bodies lie. “Which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt”: this place is spiritually called Sodom and spiritually called Egypt, because it’s the house of oppression, the house of bondage.

“And after three days and an half”: that goes back to a time, times and half a time, 350 years. “The Spirit of life from God entered into them”: we are no longer dead bodies in America. The spirit of life from God is going to enter into us. This shows the events that are going to lead up to Armageddon, with Israel.

The 350 years begin in 1619 and go to the 1960s. People had been enslaved ever since the 1400s, but in 1619 Judah was brought over here, the royal seed of King David, and the scripture says the children of Judah and Israel were oppressed together. That’s where we start counting from. That’s why in the 60s you see a lot of leaders rising up, fighting for civil rights: that was God’s spirit rising our people up. And that’s why the white man set up all type of programs to put us back to sleep and destroy the so-called black man: he introduced crack cocaine in the black community, and divided the house, the women against the husbands; that’s what Section 8 and all of that is. Exactly, it’s 1969, the turbulent 60s, when the school was set up by Abba Bivens. Ever since 1969 the truth started to be taught on the earth little by little. It started with one man, and it led up to what you see today, all of you waking up.

“And they stood upon their feet”: we stood up as the Israelites. “And great fear fell upon them which saw them”: everybody that saw us stand up as Israel became afraid.

precepts.why: What the Bible means by dead: “The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.” If you don’t have the understanding that you are an Israelite, and you’re not keeping these laws, you’re going to remain in the congregation of the dead. Those dead bodies are our people in a dead state of mind; they don’t have the spirit of God inside of them.

Why is America the great city? “And upon her forehead was a name written, MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT”. That great city is Babylon, America, “THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH.” How did we end up in Babylon? We were brought here as slaves into that great city.

sense.text: “And set me down in the midst of the valley which was full of bones”. This valley of dry bones is talking about the nation of Israel, our people. All of us at one point in time were them bones. “And, lo, they were very dry.” We read earlier that all our power was going to be taken away; that’s what the dry bones represent.
“Son of man, can these bones live? And I answered, O Lord God, thou knowest.”

“O ye dry bones, hear the word of the Lord.” “Behold, I will cause breath to enter into you, and ye shall live”. That’s after 350 years: remember, it said the spirit of life shall enter into them. That’s breath coming into us. That had to take place before Christ returns: before Armageddon takes place, we got to wake up back to who we are.

“And I will lay sinews upon you, and will bring up flesh upon you”: when flesh comes upon you, you can identify who that person is. So we start to get a little identity, trying to identify ourselves with who we are. “And put breath in you, and ye shall live; and ye shall know that I am the Lord.” This takes stages; it don’t happen overnight. In the 60s brothers were rising up and bringing the people together, but the breath wasn’t there as yet.

“And the bones came together, bone to his bone.” “The sinews and the flesh came up upon them, and the skin covered them above: but there was no breath in them.” This is the 60s. Even in the old school, brothers didn’t understand the 7-day Sabbath, that you couldn’t buy and sell; the elders weren’t fully there yet. As time went on the understanding started growing.

“Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live.” That goes into the spirit of life from God entering into us. Before Armageddon takes place, the spirit of life of God has to enter into us, and we’re already living this right here. That’s why you see Israel rising, doing the things we’re doing on the earth: the Holy Spirit has entered into us.

“And the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army.” An exceeding great army is structure and order, and the one that fits that prophecy right now, all praises to the Most High, is IUIC: the brothers and the leaders in IUIC. Not that we are the only ones teaching the truth. There’s many different Israelite groups out there putting in work too; some of them teach heresies, some of them bugged out, but the Lord is using everybody. What we’re saying is the Lord is using us to do great things on this earth, to take this truth to another level. We ain’t out there chasing a bunch of skirt, multiplying wives unto ourselves. Our focus is on the mission, not fighting and debates and arguing. We about the Lord’s business.

precepts.why:
Before Armageddon takes place, we got to wake up back to who we are. “And I saw another angel fly in the midst of heaven, having the everlasting gospel to preach unto them that dwell on the earth”. This is the time we’re living in right now: the gospel being taught right now on the earth. That’s the phase we’re in. “And to every nation, and kindred, and tongue, and people”, because Israel is scattered amongst every nation, kindred, tongue and people, so the gospel is being taught throughout the four corners of the earth.

“Saying with a loud voice, Fear God, and give glory to him”: that’s what we’re teaching in IUIC. We’re traveling the world, teaching the people who they are, to fear God and keep his commandments. “For the hour of his judgment is come”: he’s about to return. Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.

“And there followed another angel, saying, Babylon is fallen, is fallen, that great city”. Israel has to wake up and Israel has got to teach the gospel before Babylon is destroyed. First the teaching of the gospel to Israel throughout the four corners of the earth, and after that another angel prophesying Babylon is fallen. Then the third angel: “If any man worship the beast and his image, and receive his mark in his forehead, or in his hand”, the same shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God.

sense.text: This shows how the spirit of life from God entered into us. “Why then say the scribes that Elias must first come?”

“Elias truly shall first come, and restore all things.” Restore all things goes back to the remembrance of us ceasing from among men: we would forget who we are, scattered throughout the four corners of the earth. But the Bible says Elijah is going to come and restore all things, meaning Elijah is going to come and teach us who we are.

Read it again: Elias truly “shall” first come. Shall means in the future. This is talking about the last days, the 60s. That goes back to there must be a falling away first: Israel had to be scattered, Israel had to forget their nationality, the power of the holy people had to be taken. Then Elijah comes and teaches us who we are.

Bishop taught us this years ago, and we’re not 100% but it’s up there: when the Bible talks about Elijah shall come and restore things, it might be, because Christ didn’t tell us, but the prophecy fits this man: it might have been Abba Bivens. And even though it was him, he’s back again on the earth. You think he just came and restored and that’s it? No, he’s going to keep coming; he ain’t going to stop coming until Christ returns.

Abba Bivens was the leader who started the school in 1969, and under him were seven elders. These are the elders Bishop Nathanyel learned from. Out of the seven elders, a lot of them went back into the world, but we don’t speak evil of these men, because back then they did a lot for the truth. Abba was the first street teacher, and he was killed by a bunch of Muslims while teaching in the street: they jumped him and beat him bad, and he died from his injuries. Elijah came through him, or one that came through his teachings. The spirit of life entering into us came through that line, and the Bishop came from those men and is continuing the mission he was in since his 20s, and has passed what he learned down to us.

“But I say unto you, That Elias is come already”: he came already, as John the Baptist at that time, and he prepared the way for Christ. “And they knew him not, but have done unto him whatsoever they listed”: they did whatever they wanted to do to him. They killed him; they cut his head off. “Likewise shall also the Son of man suffer of them.”
“Then the disciples understood that he spake unto them of John the Baptist.” So John the Baptist was Elijah, but Christ also said Elias truly shall first come: in the future.

“So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army.” That is Israel standing up after the spirit of life from God entered into us. When you look at all of the schools that came from the original One West, that came from Bivens, they all got the truth, but who is taking the truth to another level, in terms of expansion, international teachings? It’s all about Christ using you, making yourself a vessel for Christ to use. If you’re full of hatred, envy and malice, Christ is not going to use you; you can’t be a vessel for him.

It started with Abba Bivens, he might have been Elijah; then the spirit was on Yab, Masha, Arya and the seven, and that’s where all Israel you see teaching today comes from. The Bishop came from these men, and right now the spirit is using these three men, the three Bishops, to bring the people together. It’s not us doing it on our own; it’s Christ using us. Look who’s doing the work, who’s gathering the 12 tribes, who wants Israel to come to the next level: that’s who God is using, and we cannot deny that.

Bishop has a pivotal role to play in gathering the 12 tribes of Israel together. All of us learned from him; thousands of us repented because of him, because he took this truth serious and never gave up. When it was just 10 of us sitting in a room by ourselves he kept pushing, kept teaching, and the people came. We are about taking this truth throughout the four corners of the earth and waking up Israel.

An exceeding great army: an army represents structure and order. You brothers and sisters are part of something great, and how you know it is that people speak evil of you falsely; when they speak evil and it’s a lie, you are blessed. Nobody gets more hate, ridicule and evil spoken of him than the Bishop, and knowing the things they say are not real, this man has got to have a serious role to play in these last days.

precepts.why:
“These things hast thou done, and I kept silence; thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself: but I will reprove thee”: God speaking to the white man. “And set them in order before thine eyes”: God will set the children of Israel in order. The key thing to see there is set them in order.

What you see us doing in IUIC, what the Bishops have set up, is us setting the people in order. Some people be bugging about why we search people when they come into the school, why we take a picture of people’s ID. That’s order. This is an organized nation, not some fly by night organization where you could walk up in here, give some fake name, do some evil and then disappear. When you have an organization you got to know who the hell comes through the door. Leaders understand the people depend on them, so they protect the people.

There are men, women and children in the schools in abundance, hundreds upon hundreds in a room per school. People come from different walks of life, some with psychological problems; we don’t know that at first, so we have to ask questions, are you on medications; they might do some Dylann Roof. If we set up precautionary measures to keep you safe we’re wrong for doing it, and if we don’t and someone comes up in here and shoots us up, it’s our fault for not searching. We can’t win. Some people are just going to hate until death, adverse, the opposition, as the Pharisees were to Christ, and their end will be the same as theirs.

So under the leadership of the Bishops, the deacons, captains and officers have been setting the people in order, and that’s why among us you will see structure and order.

sense.text:
What Ecclesiasticus said about Elijah: “Who anointedst kings to take revenge”: Elijah anointed kings to take revenge, “and prophets to succeed after him.” He was over schools. Elisha was the most prominent one, but there were others; he had set up schools.

So every brother, we are raising you up to succeed us. They cannot kill all of us: the spirit is going to jump from this brother to another brother, and the Most High is going to keep raising up the prophets. That’s why the Lord says he’s raising up a kingdom in the midst of this kingdom that will never be destroyed.

A lot of leaders, even Israelite leaders, are the main teacher, the only one always teaching; they are not raising up men to succeed them, so when they fall the whole thing falls apart. Same thing happened with Marcus Garvey: when he fell that movement fell; Martin Luther King, Malcolm X, because they did not set up succession. Even these holidays, the Bishop is the one who usually did them, but a couple years ago he said you all deal with that, and now the deacons take it over. precepts.why:

And when that happens, that’s when imprisonment, banishment and execution take place.

“The noise of a multitude in the mountains”: in the governments, the high powers. “Like as of a great people; a tumultuous noise”: tumultuous noise means an angry gathering, a mob, “of the kingdoms of nations gathered together”.

“The Lord of hosts mustereth the host of the battle.” The host is all the people involved in the battle. God is an instigator: when you preach that this is going to happen, I’m going to make sure it happens, just as you’re reading it and saying it.

“They come from a far country, from the end of heaven, even the Lord, and the weapons of his indignation, to destroy the whole land.” What weapon can destroy a whole land? Not a bow, not an arrow, not a catapult throwing a burning rock. Nuclear weapons, hydrogen bombs can destroy whole lands.

“Behold, saith God, I will call together all the kings of the earth to reverence me, which are from the rising of the sun”: the Far East; “from the south, from the east, and Libanus”: the near East; “to turn themselves one against another”. We read it earlier: he mustereth the battle, Isaiah 13:4-5, to destroy the whole land. The war is going to start in the East, but it’s going to end in America’s complete and total annihilation, desolation.

“And repay the things that they have done to them”: them is us. He repays them for what they have done, or will do, to us Israelites, and before that takes place it will cause us to mourn and weep and fast in our sanctuaries, making us martyrs.
“Like as they do yet this day unto my chosen”: they’re doing it now, unto us, destroying us now. “So will I do also, and recompense in their bosom.”

“My right hand shall not spare the sinners, and my sword shall not cease over them that shed innocent blood upon the earth. The fire is gone forth from his wrath, and hath consumed the foundations of the earth, and the sinners, like the straw that is kindled.” They’re going to burn.
“Woe to them that sin, and keep not my commandments!” Us too.

“Behold an horrible vision, and the appearance thereof from the east”. We keep reading it over and over: the East, the East, the East. The angel from the east saying hold back the wind, hurt not the trees and the sea; the way of the kings of the east prepared; the Euphrates dried up. It’s all about the East, the controversy of the land. Everything in this Bible revolves around the promised land and who it belongs to, and the nations that neighbor it.

“Where the nations of the dragons of Arabia”: that’s Ishmael, “shall come out with many chariots”. They are going to unify, come together, which is happening now, gradually.

“That all they which hear them may fear and tremble”: on the map, Israel is a little red dot surrounded by Muslim lands. The Arabs conquered their way across, colonized from the Northeast all the way to the Northwest, conquered the whole top half of Africa and forced us into the bottom, what they call the sub-Sahara. When they unify it’s going to be a problem, and that includes the Iranians; they’re Muslim too. Mauritania, Algeria, Morocco, Libya, Egypt, Sudan, Somalia, Yemen, the United Arab Emirates: Emirates means kings, United Arab Kings, going back to the kings of the east of Revelation 16; the twelve princes. Saudi Arabia and Oman in the middle, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, Lebanon on top: they’re surrounded.

That’s why Esau keeps them divided: he gave Saudi Arabia weapons and money, and keeps them divided through their lust for money, because he knows if they come together and start working together they can cause a problem. They got these lands by conquering, and they killed us and enslaved us before the white man enslaved us, along with the Hamites, and pushed us further south, where they call us sub-Saharan Africans now. “Also the Carmanians”: Carmania is the ancient name for Iran. “Raging in wrath shall go forth as the wild boars of the wood”, a heavy, abundant animal in that land, “and with great power shall they come, and join battle with them”: they’re going to join battle together with the Arabs, “and shall waste a portion of the land of the Assyrians”. Iran gave Israel a problem in the past; they said Iran gave Israel their Vietnam, and America got destroyed in Vietnam.
