That’s why the country became great in the first place: everybody left wherever they were and came to America, the land of liberty. The country is built on immigrants, and now they want to get rid of everybody and say there’s too many immigrants.

“But they shall not cleave one to another”: everybody’s not going to get along. There’s a division here, there will always be a division, and the division is only going to get worse. It could even fall into civil war later on down the line. Things are going to get bad here in Babylon. That is why, for fear of the oppressing sword, they shall turn every one to his people.

“We would have healed Babylon”: Trump is trying to make America, Babylon, great again; trying to heal it. “But she is not healed”, because she’s built broken. You can’t fix it; it’s already broken.

“Forsake her, and let us go every one into his own country: for her judgment reacheth unto heaven, and is lifted up even to the skies.” Everyone going to leave here, every one to his own land.

“A sword is upon their horses”: that goes into their cars, their businesses, their companies. “And upon their chariots, and upon all the mingled people that are in the midst of her”, the nations heaped together in her, “and they shall become as women.” When danger takes place, what do women do? They run. They’re going to run and leave the country.

“A sword is upon her treasures”: all that money that gets made here is going to be gone; the stock exchange, crypto, done. “And they shall be robbed”: they ain’t going to have no money. They got to leave out of here broke.

sense.text:
“Behold, a people shall come from the north”: that goes into Russia, that goes into Iran, and the EU, the European Union. “And a great nation, and many kings shall be raised up from the coasts of the earth”: from every part of the earth. They’re going to unify against America.

This is referring to NATO, the European Union. Write that down: NATO.

“They are cruel, and will not shew mercy”: to Babylon. They’re going to drop every bomb they can. “Their voice shall roar like the sea”: there be many of them. “Every one put in array, like a man to the battle, against thee, O daughter of Babylon.”

“The king of Babylon hath heard the report of them”: that’s the president. The EU has turned against her, Russia turned against her: oh man, I thought we was cool, what happened? The president is going to know when they betray America and when they’re about to destroy America; they can tell when a missile is shot half an hour before it reaches you.

“And his hands waxed feeble”: America cannot stop all those nukes; they cannot defend against them. “Anguish took hold of him, and pangs as of a woman in travail”: he goes to that bunker.

“Behold, he shall come up like a lion from the swelling of Jordan unto the habitation of the strong”: America will try to assist Israel when this war is breaking loose. Babylon’s symbol was the lion; that’s America, going toward Jordan.

“But I will make them suddenly run away from her”: he will make America run away from the EU. The EU is going to attack America when she is trying to defend Israel. When the northern army goes over there and America comes to defend Israel, that’s when the EU, NATO, is going to strike America, when her defenses are down and she least expects it. They’re going to try to retreat and defend America, but it’ll be too late.

“And who is a chosen man, that I may appoint over her? for who is like me? and who will appoint me the time? and who is that shepherd that will stand before me?” He’s referring to his visitation. America is not destroyed fully until the end: Christ is going to return and deliver the finishing blow. Only I am the one who will destroy America completely in the end.

“Therefore hear ye the counsel of the Lord, that he hath taken against Babylon”: he’s saying it again, the same as Jeremiah 49:20. “Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out”: the least of the flock is Israel. Draw them out: that goes into NATO attacking America; Israel, Iran, China, all the nations fighting against America. “Surely he shall make their habitation desolate with them”: bombs will be hitting from all different directions.

“At the noise of the taking of Babylon the earth is moved, and the cry is heard among the nations”: Ashkelon going to see it, Gaza going to see it, everybody is going to see it, and Babylon will be completely destroyed.

This can’t be ancient Babylon. When the Medes and the Persians conquered the old Babylon, the earth didn’t move for anything; it was an inside job, it was taken over from the inside, pretty much a peaceful takeover. So it’s not the same Babylon. This is the new Babylon, the modern one.

precepts.why:
“Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof. O daughter of Babylon, who art to be destroyed.”

So Edom is called of old the daughter of Babylon. That is why it said earlier that Babylon last broke our bones: it is referring to Edom. And this people from the north come in array against thee, O daughter of Babylon: against Edom.

sense.text: “Behold, I will raise up against Babylon, and against them that dwell in the midst of them that rise up against me, a destroying wind”: the destroying wind is the militaries, the armies of the nations.
“And will send unto Babylon fanners, that shall fan her”: a fanner keeps the flame burning; fanners keep the fire going. “For in the day of trouble they shall be against her round about.”
“Spare ye not her young men; destroy ye utterly all her host”: all the bombs on her host, her armies, on the land entirely.
“Thus the slain shall fall in the land of the Chaldeans, and they that are thrust through in her streets”: they’re going to bomb all the cities; people are going to be destroyed.
“For Israel hath not been forsaken, nor Judah of his God, of the Lord of hosts; though their land was filled with sin against the Holy One of Israel.”

“Flee out of the midst of Babylon, and deliver every man his soul: be not cut off in her iniquity; for this is the time of the Lord’s vengeance”: don’t be destroyed along with the rest of the inhabitants. Don’t be involved in America’s sins. Make sure you’re found worthy and righteous in that time when that happens.

precepts.why: Touched on earlier with Revelation 7:3; verse 1 explains the destroying wind. “And after these things I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth”: holding the four winds, the destroying winds. That is the militaries, the armies of the nations.

sense.text:
“Make bright the arrows; gather the shields: the Lord hath raised up the spirit of the kings of the Medes”: that’s Iran. Remember Iran and Russia are next door. “For his device is against Babylon, to destroy it; because it is the vengeance of the Lord, the vengeance of his temple.”

We know who is going to destroy America: the Medes. Remember what was said early on: look on the US dollar and you see that six-point star. The United States of America and Israel is one. Everything is going to pop off over there first. Iran is going to fight over there; the Medes are going to rise up and fight against America and Israel over there in the East. What was read earlier, that’s when the war is taken to the land over here itself; but what we read here is America and Israel fighting over there in the East.

precepts.why:
Just to back it up: “Behold, I will stir up the Medes against them, which shall not regard silver; and as for gold, they shall not delight in it.” They ain’t going to care about money no more. You ain’t buying them off; no trade, none of that. “Their bows also shall dash the young men to pieces; and they shall have no pity on the fruit of the womb; their eye shall not spare children.” “And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms”, “shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah”: bombs dropping. That is the same thing read in Jeremiah 51:25, I will make thee a burnt mountain. It goes both ways.

“Their children also shall be dashed to pieces before their eyes”: that goes with the verse that says they ain’t going to show no pity to the fruit of the womb. Who is going to be doing this? The Arabs and the Medes, the Iranians. “Their houses shall be spoiled”: is this talking about here in America? No, it’s talking about the land of Israel. “And their wives ravished”: their wives going to be raped.

So it is talking about Babylon, but it is the land of Israel. A lot of the time, when the prophecy talks about Babylon it is interchangeable. When you read Obadiah, that’s talking about America and Israel. They go hand in hand; they work together; they are one.

To prove it’s talking about the land of Israel: “For I will gather all nations against Jerusalem to battle”. That’s what Deacon Eythan has been touching on: the Most High God is going to gather all nations down in Jerusalem to battle, including America. America is going to be over there supporting Israel.

“And the city shall be taken”: the city of Israel is going to be taken. Those white people that’s controlling that land today will lose it; that’s the prophecy. “And the houses rifled”: isn’t that the same thing we just read in Isaiah 13? So it’s talking about Jerusalem, the land of Israel. Why? Because who is occupying the land of Israel? Esau, America. They are one.

“And the women ravished”: the women are going to be raped. “And half of the city shall go forth into captivity”: half of the city is going to become prisoners of war. This is Bible prophecy: eventually the Israelis are going to lose them cities. They going to lose Jerusalem to the Arabs.

sense.text:
“Behold, I am against thee, O destroying mountain, saith the Lord, which destroyest all the earth”: destroys the air, destroys the animals, destroys people, destroys the water, destroys the crops. It pollutes the earth, pollutes the air, the land, sea and air, and the people.

This goes back to Isaiah 13:19 and down. “And I will stretch out mine hand upon thee, and roll thee down from the rocks”: remove your power. “And will make thee a burnt mountain”: as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.

“And they shall not take of thee a stone for a corner, nor a stone for foundations”: nothing will be left. “But thou shalt be desolate for ever, saith the Lord”: that’s Isaiah 13, the same exact thing.

“Set ye up a standard in the land, blow the trumpet among the nations, prepare the nations against her”: against America and Israel. “Call together against her the kingdoms of Ararat”: Ararat is Turkey. Minni is the same area, and Ashchenaz will be around Germany; it goes back to the EU. “Appoint a captain against her; cause the horses to come up as the rough caterpillers”: they’re going to be getting attacked from the inside also.

“Prepare against her the nations with the kings of the Medes, the captains thereof, and all the rulers thereof, and all the land of his dominion”: they’re going to be attacked at the same time. When they come to defend Israel, they’re going to strike America; then they’re going to try to run back and defend it, but it’ll be too late. They’ll be gone.

precepts.why:
When you go further down, Isaiah 13 is going into America. Prove it: “And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldees’ excellency, shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah. It shall never be inhabited”, so we know it’s not referring to Israel; Israel is going to be inhabited. “Neither shall it be dwelt in from generation to generation”: so that ain’t Israel. “Neither shall the Arabian pitch tent there; neither shall the shepherds make their fold there. But wild beasts of the desert shall lie there; and their houses shall be full of doleful creatures; and owls shall dwell there, and satyrs shall dance there. And the wild beasts of the islands shall cry in their desolate houses, and dragons in their pleasant palaces: and her time is near to come, and her days shall not be prolonged.”

That right there is America. And Jeremiah 51:25 is the same exact thing: the destroying mountain made a burnt mountain, as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, desolate for ever.

sense.text: “And from the land of the Assyrians shall the enemy besiege them”: we read earlier about the Arabs coming together with the Carmanians and gaining the upper hand, and the cities where they ravish the women. “And in their host shall be fear and dread, and strife among their kings”: between Israel and these two nations.

“Behold clouds from the east”: that goes to China, Japan, North Korea, that area. “And from the north”: that’s Russia, the European area. “Unto the south”: the south goes back to Saudi Arabia, the Middle East there. “And they are very horrible to look upon, full of wrath and storm”: wrath and storm means military.

“They shall smite one upon another”: missiles hitting them, missiles going back and forth. “And they shall smite down a great multitude of stars upon the earth”: they’re going to be fighting against Israel; that’s the so-called Iron Dome trying to knock down the missiles. Watch the news: the Iron Dome cannot defend against a lot of missiles; it is not that strong. “Even their own star”: their own star won’t make it; it gets destroyed. “And blood shall be from the sword unto the belly”: it’s going to be a lot of death.
“And dung of men unto the camel’s hough”: dung of men means the guts. Guts and blood everywhere, dead bodies everywhere, mutilated everywhere.
“And then shall there come great storms from the south, and from the north, and another part from the west”: the west is America.

“And strong winds shall arise from the east, and shall open it”: the silo; the missiles coming out the silo. “And the cloud which he raised up in wrath”: that’s going into the EU, NATO. “And the star stirred to cause fear toward the east and west wind, shall be destroyed”: that star won’t make it. They’re going to try to shoot it. There’ll be fear, but it’ll be destroyed.

“The great and mighty clouds”: clouds, more than one. The clouds are NATO, the European nations. “And the star, that they may make all the earth afraid”: that’s the ICBM, a nuclear weapon, a powerful one that makes all the earth afraid just knowing about it. “And they shall pour out over every high and eminent place an horrible star”: they’re going to shoot multiples of those ICBMs.

“Fire, and hail, and flying swords”: missiles; flying swords are hypersonic missiles. “And many waters, that all fields may be full, and all rivers, with the abundance of great waters”: they’re going to knock buildings down, and it’s going to be floods, lots of water coming in, radiated water. It will be flooded.

“And they shall break down the cities and walls, mountains and hills, trees of the wood, and grass of the meadows, and their corn.” Remember Revelation 7: the winds were held back so they wouldn’t hurt the trees nor the sea. This is the trees getting hurt and the sea being hurt.

“And they shall go stedfastly unto Babylon, and make her afraid”: the stars, the fire and hail and flying swords go steadfastly unto Babylon. While war is taking place in the near East, the horrible star is going to be shot steadfastly into Babylon.

“They shall come to her, and besiege her”: there’s going to be a bunch of missiles hitting her at one time. “The star and all wrath shall they pour out upon her”: that same terrible star that makes all the earth afraid in verse 40. They’re all going to shoot at her at once, the NATO. “Then shall the dust and smoke go up unto the heaven, and all they that be about her shall bewail her.”

precepts.why:
Going back to the clouds hitting Babylon steadfastly. “Behold, a people shall come from the north”: remember the clouds from the north. “And a great nation”: that’s the great clouds. “And many kings shall be raised up from the coasts of the earth”: the many kings are the clouds, north, south, east, west.

“They shall hold the bow and the lance: they are cruel, and will not shew mercy”: that is why they go steadfast to Babylon. Show no mercy: they’re going to shoot everything they got at Babylon, over every high and eminent place, dropping bombs everywhere. Steadfastly means directly; they ain’t making no turns. They all going to target Babylon, America, to destroy her entirely. All reasoning is going to be gone; they won’t care what happens after. They’ll be minded, we got to destroy the whole continent of America. Today Putin makes little threats about using nuclear weapons; at that time all reasoning is going to leave them, and they’re going to just start letting off nuclear bombs in America.

“A people shall come from the north”: we know NATO is up there, but guess who is up there also: Russia. What role has Russia got to play in all of this? Russia has about the same amount of nuclear weapons America have. America is trying to come out of NATO, and NATO may form an alliance with Russia in the future, because it says from the north. So Russia is involved in them clouds.

sense.text: “Then saw I a dream, and, behold, there came up from the sea an eagle, which had twelve feathered wings, and three heads.” This is the animal Daniel did not see in Daniel 7. He saw the lion, he saw the bear and he saw the leopard, but he did not describe the fourth beast. The Lord revealed to Ezra the fourth beast: the eagle with twelve feathered wings and three heads. Remember the symbol of the eagle is Rome: Greece, the white man, Edom.
“And I saw, and, behold, she spread her wings over all the earth, and all the winds of the air blew on her, and were gathered together”: all nations gathered to her.

“But her heads were at rest”: it wasn’t time for them to come into power yet. “The head in the midst was greater than the other”: write this down. There’s three heads, and the head in the middle is Rome.
“Watch not all at once: sleep every one in his own place, and watch by course”: they all come into power at different times.
“But let the heads be preserved for the last.”

“And I beheld, and, lo, the voice went not out of her heads, but from the midst of her body”: the midst of her body goes back to them secret societies, all of them that run things behind the scenes. They speak secretly.

precepts.why:
“After this I looked, and, behold, the twelve feathers appeared no more”: the twelve feathers are the twelve Caesars, the twelve Kaisers, Julius all the way down to Domitian. They’re all dead and gone. “Nor the two little feathers”: besides the twelve main feathers there were eight contrary feathers.

“And there was no more upon the eagle’s body, but three heads that rested, and six little wings”: of the eight, two were gone and six were left. “Then saw I also that two little feathers divided themselves from the six, and remained under the head that was upon the right side”: two little feathers moved themselves onto the head on the right side.

The right side is the European Union, NATO; that’s the right head. The big head is Rome, in the front. America, Babylon, is the head to the left. That’s three: Rome in the front, the stout and great, Great Britain and NATO, the EU, on the right, and America on the left. And the little feathers, Russia, went over to that right side. “For the four continued in their place”: they continued in the Dark Ages.

“And when they so thought, behold, there awaked one of the heads that were at rest, namely, it that was in the midst; for that was greater than the two other heads”: there was a main head, and that was Rome. “And then I saw that the two other heads were joined with it. And, behold, the head was turned with them that were with it, and did eat up the two feathers under the wing that would have reigned. But this head put the whole earth in fear, and bare rule in it over all those that dwelt upon the earth with much oppression; and it had the governance of the world more than all the wings that had been.”

Where the heads eat each other. “In his last days shall the most High raise up three kingdoms, and renew many things therein, and they shall have the dominion of the earth, And of those that dwell therein, with much oppression, above all those that were before them: therefore are they called the heads of the eagle. For these are they that shall accomplish his wickedness, and that shall finish his last end.”

“And whereas thou sawest that the great head appeared no more”: the great head is Rome; Rome is gone now. “It signifieth that one of them shall die upon his bed, and yet with pain. For the two that remain shall be slain with the sword. For the sword of the one shall devour the other”: one head will devour the other. “But at the last shall he fall through the sword himself.”

“And whereas thou sawest two feathers under the wings passing over the head that is on the right side”: those two feathers on the right hand side are Russia, allied with the EU. Those two little feathers are Gog and Magog. So one head devours the other with the help of those two feathers: the EU, NATO and Russia. “It signifieth that these are they, whom the Highest hath kept unto their end: this is the small kingdom and full of trouble”: that goes into Ezekiel 38 and 39, where they’re going to rouse the nations to fight against the Lord and against us while we’re in our safety. That’s Gog and Magog, the little kingdom.

sense.text: “And therefore, saith the Lord, I will surely avenge them”: avenge us. “And receive unto me all the innocent blood from among them”: they’re going to make us martyrs.

“Behold, my people is led as a flock to the slaughter”: they’re going to be killing us; the northern army. “I will not suffer them now to dwell in the land of Egypt”: remember the horrible star of verses 40 to 44 regarding Babylon. Egypt is also America: the land of Egypt, spiritual Egypt.

“But I will bring them with a mighty hand and a stretched out arm, and smite Egypt with plagues, as before, and will destroy all the land thereof.” That goes back to Isaiah 13:5: they still head steadfastly to Babylon and destroy her, and the smoke goes up into heaven as in verse 44. It’s the same thing.

“They that till the ground shall mourn: for their seeds shall fail through the blasting and hail, and with a fearful constellation.” The fearful constellation is a fearful star, the same horrible star of verses 40 to 44; a constellation is a star. So it is referring to America being destroyed: Egypt in one place, Babylon in verse 43, and the horrible star and the fearful constellation are synonymous.

“Woe to the world and them that dwell therein!” For one people shall stand up against another, with “swords in their hands”: swords in their hands goes back to nuclear weapons, warheads. The earlier verses of chapter 15 are an introduction to the rest of the chapter.

Christ said nation against nation, kingdom against kingdom. That’s the time now.

precepts.why: What is Babylon referred to as? “And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city”: the great city is Babylon, “which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt”. So when Ezra says I will not suffer them now to dwell in the land of Egypt, it is spiritual Egypt: Babylon, America.

Going back to the horrible star, the fearful constellation, and how they go steadfastly unto Babylon to make her afraid. This goes into two things: Egypt being smitten and destroyed, or Babylon being steadfastly destroyed by the horrible star; and also the eagle with three heads, one head devouring the other with the help of the two feathers, Gog and Magog, Russia.

“The waters which thou sawest, where the whore sitteth, are peoples, and multitudes, and nations, and tongues.” “And the ten horns which thou sawest upon the beast”: the ten horns go back to those kings, the ones in the north, those great clouds, plural. “These shall hate the whore”, and attack her without mercy: that’s Jeremiah 50:41-42 and 2 Esdras 15:40-44. “And shall make her desolate and naked”: desolate with what? With a fearful constellation, with a horrible star, where the smoke shall ascend up, as in 2 Esdras 15:44. “And shall eat her flesh, and burn her with fire”: Babylon will be a burnt mountain.

“For God hath put in their hearts to fulfil his will”: as Isaiah 13 says, the Lord musters the battle, the gathering of the nations to destroy the whole land. “And to agree, and give their kingdom unto the beast”: they did it after World War II, all together, NATO and the EU. But now that’s all starting to come apart. “Until the words of God shall be fulfilled”: then they turn against her.

The new president is already saying y’all in NATO have to pay up; y’all been playing games all this time, pay the master. Trump has a big role to play in America leaving NATO; Trump is fulfilling prophecies. NATO and the European nations gave their power over to America for a time, and that time is up. In the White House years ago he told the alliance that 23 of the 28 member nations were not paying their fair share for their defense. And now Trump is back, and within his time prophecies are going to be fulfilled.

sense.text: “They shall come to her, and besiege her, the star and all wrath shall they pour out upon her”: remember the great constellation against Egypt; it’s the same on Babylon, the same place. “Then shall the dust and smoke go up unto the heaven, and all they that be about her shall bewail her.”

precepts.why: “And after these things I saw another angel come down from heaven, having great power; and the earth was lightened with his glory. And he cried mightily with a strong voice, saying, Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird.” You got that exact same thing in Isaiah 13:19: desolate.

“For in one hour so great riches is come to nought. And every shipmaster, and all the company in ships, and sailors, and as many as trade by sea, stood afar off, And cried when they saw the smoke of her burning”. The smoke of her burning is the dust and smoke going up unto the heaven when the star and all wrath are poured out upon her.

“And the kings of the earth, who have committed fornication and lived deliciously with her, shall bewail her”: that’s 2 Esdras 15:44 saying the exact same thing, all they that be about her shall bewail her. “And lament for her, when they shall see the smoke of her burning, Standing afar off for the fear of her torment, saying, Alas, alas, that great city Babylon, that mighty city! for in one hour is thy judgment come.” That’s the exact same thing in 2 Esdras 15. This is war.

A scripture concerning Revelation 18. “Take a good heart, O Jerusalem: for he that gave thee that name will comfort thee. Miserable are they that afflicted thee”: everybody that afflicted the twelve tribes of Israel, that had us as slaves, God said they going to be miserable. “And rejoiced at thy fall.”

“Miserable are the cities which thy children served”: did we serve slavery in America? Did we serve slavery in Europe, in Spain, in all these countries? Whatever country had us as slaves, God says miserable are these cities. “Miserable is she that received thy sons”: anybody that touched us, anybody that had Israel as slaves, judgment is coming on them from the Lord.

“For as she rejoiced at thy ruin, and was glad of thy fall”: that’s what Christmas is all about; they made merry and rejoiced at our fall. “So shall she be grieved for her own desolation”: there’s going to be desolation taking place in America. “For I will take away the rejoicing of her great multitude”: there ain’t going to be no more rejoicing here in America, in Babylon. “And her pride shall be turned into mourning. For fire shall come upon her from the Everlasting, long to endure”: that’s what we just read in Revelation 17, burn her with fire. “And she shall be inhabited of devils for a great time”: the same thing we read in Revelation 18, the habitation of devils.

All these wars are about the Lord delivering us out of this captivity, and delivering our land out of our enemies too, and at the same time killing our enemies and giving us the land.

“The vision of Obadiah. Thus saith the Lord God concerning Edom; We have heard a rumour from the Lord, and an ambassador is sent among the heathen, Arise ye, and let us rise up against her in battle”: that goes back to the Middle East, Iran, the Arabs.

“How are the things of Esau searched out! how are his hidden things sought up!” Over time he’ll be exposed as the devil he is, the wicked the Bible speaks of, through our teachings.

“All the men of thy confederacy”: the EU, NATO; Revelation 17, they shall hate the whore. Confederacy goes back to what Trump said: the alliance. “Have brought thee even to the border: the men that were at peace with thee have deceived thee”: when America goes to defend Israel, the EU is going to attack America at the same time. “And prevailed against thee”: they destroy you utterly; the land is utterly destroyed and the smoke goes up. Baruch said it, Ezra saw it, Isaiah saw it, Obadiah saw it, Jeremiah saw it.

“They that eat thy bread have laid a wound under thee”: they that are with you, your allies, turn their back on you. “There is none understanding in him”: your wisdom is gone. Normally he would see it, but at this point the Most High is going to say no, you ain’t going to see it coming. He’s going to blind them.

Esau’s main thing is to take and maintain precedence over that land: keep us in captivity and keep our land in their possession. But they’re going to lose both. When the bombs come over this side of the world we get delivered; they come back over here to defend it, and they get bombed over there. They’re going to get hit in both directions.

sense.text: Remember what Christ said: he’s going to visit Teman. I’m going to visit you. “Then the eleven disciples went away into Galilee, into a mountain where Jesus had appointed them”: keep in mind he told the disciples to meet him at a mountain where he appointed them.

“And Jesus came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.” When Christ died, the Lord said good job; now when the time comes you will go and take what’s yours. That is all power.

precepts.why: “Afterward he appeared unto the eleven as they sat at meat, and upbraided them with their unbelief and hardness of heart”: he cursed them out for not believing, “because they believed not them which had seen him after he was risen.” “And he said unto them, Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature”: where Israel is found. “He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved; but he that believeth not shall be damned.”

“So then after the Lord had spoken unto them, he was received up into heaven, and sat on the right hand of God. And they went forth, and preached every where, the Lord working with them, and confirming the word with signs following.” Mark 16 is pretty much the introduction to Acts chapter 1; it is a precept to Acts 1.

He said meet me at this mountain, and from that same mountain he flew up from them. “And he led them out as far as to Bethany”: that same mountain. “And he lifted up his hands, and blessed them. And it came to pass, while he blessed them, he was parted from them, and carried up into heaven.”
Where is Bethany? “And when they came nigh to Jerusalem, unto Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount of Olives”. Bethany is at the Mount of Olives.

“And when he had spoken these things, while they beheld, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight”: he flew up into the Chariot. “And while they looked stedfastly toward heaven as he went up, behold, two men stood by them in white apparel; Which also said, Ye men of Galilee, why stand ye gazing up into heaven?” What you looking for?

“This same Jesus, which is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven”: the same way you saw him fly up, in his place, you’re going to see him come right back down to this place.

“Then returned they unto Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet”: so Christ flew up from them at the Mount of Olives. The mountain where he appointed them is the place he ascended from, and he will descend again at the exact same spot.

sense.text: “For I will gather all nations against Jerusalem to battle”: Armageddon. “And the city shall be taken, and the houses rifled”: that goes back to Israel being overthrown by the Arabs and the Carmanians. “And the women ravished”: go back to Isaiah 13. “And half of the city shall go forth into captivity”: war captives. “And the residue of the people shall not be cut off from the city”: not all of them will be killed out of there, not yet.
“Then shall the Lord go forth, and fight against those nations”: during that battle. “As when he fought in the day of battle”: going back to the Exodus from Egypt.

“And his feet shall stand in that day upon the mount of Olives”: when he left the disciples it was at the Mount of Olives, and when he comes back down he’s going to land in the exact same spot, in the near East, “which is before Jerusalem on the east”.

“And the mount of Olives shall cleave in the midst thereof toward the east and toward the west”: when he lands on it the mountain will break in pieces, divided in half. “And there shall be a very great valley”: because the mountain is divided in half, there will be a big path in between. “And half of the mountain shall remove toward the north, and half of it toward the south”: it’s going to split into four pieces when he lands on it.

“And ye shall flee to the valley of the mountains”: they’re going to flee when he arrives; they’re going to run when he lands. “Yea, ye shall flee, like as ye fled from before the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah: and the Lord my God shall come, and all the saints with thee”: and all his angels with him, his legions with him.

precepts.why: “And in that day will I make Jerusalem a burdensome stone for all people: all that burden themselves with it shall be cut in pieces, though all the people of the earth be gathered together against it.” All the people of the earth gathered against Jerusalem: that is the battle he lands in.

He told them to flee: flee by Teman and Dedan. “Concerning Edom, thus saith the Lord of hosts; Is wisdom no more in Teman? is counsel perished from the prudent? is their wisdom vanished?” Why does he ask that question? Read the next verse.

“Flee ye, turn back, dwell deep, O inhabitants of Dedan”: they’re going to run, as in Zechariah 14. “For I will bring the calamity of Esau upon him”: he lands on the Mount of Olives and brings Esau’s calamity himself. “The time that I will visit him”: the time that I land on the Mount of Olives I’m going to do damage; I’m going to finish them off. That’s the visit to Teman that Christ spoke of.

sense.text: Remember he said, is wisdom no more in Teman: Dedan is going to flee when Christ lands on the Mount of Olives and cleaves the mountain in four places. “O Lord, I have heard thy speech, and was afraid: O Lord, revive thy work in the midst of the years”: the Lord’s work. “In the midst of the years make known”: make things known to us. Making known goes back to turning the heart of the fathers to the children and the children to the fathers. “In wrath remember mercy.”

“God came from Teman”: who came from Teman? God. Teman goes to the Mount of Olives; when he landed on the Mount of Olives. “And the Holy One from mount Paran”: in that same area. “His glory covered the heavens, and the earth was full of his praise.”

Put the maps up and you see the Mount of Olives is right there, close to Edom. They’re next door; he’s going there for a reason. Lebanon is above Jerusalem and Teman is right under it, so it’s next door; maybe about 60 miles off, very close. Teman is there, Edom right there, Dedan is right in that area, and Bozrah is all that area. Keep that in mind.

“And his brightness was as the light”: he had power all around his body, like them chariots, radiant energy. “He had horns coming out of his hand”: he had beams of light in his hand like a superhero. “And there was the hiding of his power”: he had to hold back, because he would destroy every damn thing.
“Before him went the pestilence, and burning coals went forth at his feet”: so when he landed he caused the earthquake, and everything melted under his feet.

“Was the Lord displeased against the rivers?” Yes, he was. “Was thine anger against the rivers? was thy wrath against the sea”: the nations. “That thou didst ride upon thine horses and thy chariots of salvation?” He is going to ride upon a chariot. He’s going to come with his Chariot; he’s going to bring his car with him.

“Thou didst cleave the earth with rivers. The mountains saw thee, and they trembled”: they split in four. “The overflowing of the water passed by: the deep uttered his voice, and lifted up his hands on high.”
“Thou didst march through the land in indignation, thou didst thresh the heathen in anger.”

“Thou wentest forth for the salvation of thy people, even for salvation with thine anointed”, against “the head out of the house of the wicked”: the house of the thief. “By discovering the foundation unto the neck”: he cut the entire head off. Christ finishes Esau off himself.
“They came out as a whirlwind to scatter me”: they ain’t going to beat him. “Their rejoicing was as to devour the poor secretly”: they tried to destroy us secretly.

“When I heard, my belly trembled; my lips quivered at the voice: rottenness entered into my bones, and I trembled in myself, that I might rest in the day of trouble”: he prayed he was dead during that time. I want to see that in real life. “When he cometh up unto the people, he will invade them with his troops”: he will come with his saints, as in Zechariah 14.

precepts.why:
“Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah?” From Bozrah, not too far from the Mount of Olives. “This that is glorious in his apparel, travelling in the greatness of his strength? I that speak in righteousness, mighty to save. Wherefore art thou red in thine apparel”: why are your garments covered in red? “And thy garments like him that treadeth in the winefat?”

“I have trodden the winepress alone”: I’m going to do it alone; I don’t need help. “And of the people there was none with me: for I will tread them in mine anger, and trample them in my fury; and their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments, and I will stain all my raiment. For the day of vengeance is in mine heart, and the year of my redeemed is come”: the year of our redemption.

“Come near, ye nations, to hear; and hearken, ye people”. “For the indignation of the Lord is upon all nations, and his fury upon all their armies: he hath utterly destroyed them”: because they’re all going to end up in the valley of Jehoshaphat, and he’s going to destroy them all in that valley. “He hath delivered them to the slaughter. Their slain also shall be cast out, and their stink shall come up out of their carcases, and the mountains shall be melted with their blood”: that goes back to the northern army getting destroyed too.

“And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved, and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll”: bombs dropping, destruction. “And all their host shall fall down, as the leaf falleth off from the vine, and as a falling fig from the fig tree. For my sword shall be bathed in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Idumea”: Edom, “and upon the people of my curse, to judgment.”

“The sword of the Lord is filled with blood, it is made fat with fatness, and with the blood of lambs and goats, with the fat of the kidneys of rams: for the Lord hath a sacrifice in Bozrah”, close to Teman and the Mount of Olives, “and a great slaughter in the land of Idumea.” “For it is the day of the Lord’s vengeance, and the year of recompences for the controversy of Zion. And the streams thereof shall be turned into pitch, and the dust thereof into brimstone.”

“It shall not be quenched night nor day; the smoke thereof shall go up for ever: from generation to generation it shall lie waste; none shall pass through it for ever and ever”: that’s America. “But the cormorant and the bittern shall possess it”: those are fowls. “The owl also and the raven shall dwell in it: and he shall stretch out upon it the line of confusion”: because it’s a land of confusion, “and the stones of emptiness.” “And thorns shall come up in her palaces, nettles and brambles in the fortresses thereof: and it shall be an habitation of dragons”: a habitation of devils, as in Revelation 18:2 and Isaiah 13:19 and down, “and a court for owls.”

sense.text: “And after this I beheld, and, lo, there was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea”: the man that came out of the sky, that lands on the Mount of Olives.
“But I beheld, and, lo, he had graved himself a great mountain, and flew up upon it”: he did what? Flew up upon it, because he can fly.
“But I would have seen the region or place whereout the hill was graven, and I could not”: he didn’t know what the mountain was yet.
“All they which were gathered together to subdue him were sore afraid”: they were terrified of him. Yet they fought him anyway.

“He neither lifted up his hand, nor held sword, nor any instrument of war: But only I saw that he sent out of his mouth as it had been a blast of fire, and out of his lips a flaming breath, and out of his tongue he cast out sparks and tempests”: he burned them all alive. “And they were all mixed together; the blast of fire, the flaming breath, and the great tempest; and fell with violence upon the multitude which was prepared to fight, and burned them up every one, so that upon a sudden of an innumerable multitude nothing was to be perceived, but only dust and smell of smoke.”

Ezra saw them all get burned up. Isaiah saw him kill them with the sword, slashing them to pieces, destroying everything; Ezra sees him burn them with his mouth.
“Afterward saw I the same man come down from the mountain, and call unto him another peaceable Multitude”: the northern kingdom of Israel.

precepts.why:
“This is the meaning of the vision: Whereas thou sawest a man coming up from the midst of the sea”: the sea is space. “The same is he whom God the Highest hath kept a great season, which by his own self shall deliver his creature”: the Israelites, all over the earth. “And he shall order them that are left behind”: that are saved. He held “neither sword, nor any instrument of war, but that the rushing in of him destroyed the whole multitude that came to subdue him”.

“Behold, the days come, when the most High will begin to deliver them that are upon the earth. And he shall come to the astonishment of them that dwell on the earth”: he’ll show up in that Chariot, like they see all the time in Jersey, only bigger. “And one shall undertake to fight against another, one city against another, one place against another, one people against another, and one realm against another”: this verse explains 2 Esdras 15, the entire chapter; it is going into what happens before America is destroyed.

“And then shall my Son be declared, whom thou sawest as a man ascending”: who you saw as a man flying. “And when all the people hear his voice, every man shall in their own land leave the battle they have one against another”: after they nuke America to hell, and the Navy goes back and forth fighting with Iran and the Arabs and Israel, they’re going to stop fighting each other and turn their eyes on the Lord, “willing to come, and to overcome him by fighting.”

“But he shall stand upon the top of the mount Sion. And Sion shall come, and shall be shewed to all men, being prepared and builded, like as thou sawest the hill graven without hands”: that’s us. “And this my Son shall rebuke the wicked inventions of those nations”: Esau is going to bring out his heaviest, most amazing technology, and it’s going to do nothing at all. “Which for their wicked life are fallen into the tempest; And shall lay before them their evil thoughts, and the torments wherewith they shall begin to be tormented, which are like unto a flame”: and he shall destroy them without labour.

“And whereas thou sawest that he gathered another peaceable multitude unto him”: the northern kingdom.

“Now when he destroyeth the multitude of the nations that are gathered together, he shall defend his people that remain”: he will defend us that remain after that. “And then shall he shew them great wonders”: he will show us amazing wonders, things you never thought or seen before, when he delivers us.

“Then said I, O Lord that bearest rule, shew me this: Wherefore have I seen the man coming up from the midst of the sea?” Who is this I saw flying, who came from space? “Like as thou canst neither seek out nor know the things that are in the deep of the sea: even so can no man upon earth see my Son, or those that be with him, but in the daytime”: in the light, walking in the light of the commandments. “This is the interpretation of the dream which thou sawest”: we are enlightened to read this and understand it.

“For thou hast forsaken thine own way”: we have forsaken our own way. We’re not keeping New Year’s, we’re not keeping Christmas, Thanksgiving. “And applied thy diligence unto my law, and sought it”: we apply our diligence to God’s law and seek after it. “Thy life hast thou ordered in wisdom”: in this room we are trying to order our lives in wisdom, “and hast called understanding thy mother. And therefore have I shewed thee the treasures of the Highest”: the Most High showed all of us in this room the treasures of the Highest. “After other three days I will speak other things unto thee, and declare unto thee mighty and wondrous things. Then went I forth into the field, giving praise and thanks greatly unto the most High because of his wonders, which he did in time”.
